interpretations: Filter tracks with Bytes > 10,323,804 (strict). Per media type, compute the average of (Bytes ÷ Milliseconds) across its tracks. Then take the simple (unweighted) mean of those per-media-type averages. Group by media type name and join to MediaType, so only media types with qualifying tracks are included.
Same as 1, but the filter is Bytes >= 10,323,804 (inclusive).
Same as 1, but the per-type average is the ratio of sums (SUM(Bytes) ÷ SUM(Milliseconds)), not the mean of per-track ratios.
Same as 1, but integer division is used for Bytes ÷ Milliseconds, so each track's ratio is truncated to a whole number before averaging.
Same as 1, but the grouping uses MediaTypeId rather than the name. This gives the same result unless two media types share a name.
Same as 1, but media types with no qualifying tracks are included, with an average of 0 or NULL. This changes the final mean if zeros are counted.
Same as 1, but the final average is weighted by the number of tracks per media type, not a simple average of the per-type averages.
Same as 1, but tracks with NULL Bytes are handled explicitly. They are excluded by the filter anyway.
Same as 1, but tracks with Milliseconds equal to 0 are excluded to avoid division by zero. Milliseconds is NOT NULL.
Same as 1, but "bytes per millisecond" is read as Milliseconds ÷ Bytes (the inverse ratio).
Same as 1, but the 10,323,804 threshold is applied to a different quantity, such as media type totals, album totals, or the average file size, instead of to each track's Bytes.
Same as 1, but the result is returned with full floating-point precision and no rounding, as the question states. A different rounding would be a separate reading.
